grammar.rule: The first binder establishes x,H,b,I. The delayed INDEX at .1G7 identifies the same x throughout this paragraph. This is a paid paragraph-scope law, not a visible prose-to-star pointer.

Core ch+t+eey returns Event[positive height derivative]; ch+o+t+eey returns Event[negative height derivative]; ch+eey returns State[height]. Nominalization has a declared tagged sum State|Event and no mixed-class cast.

Typed o flips orientation of a change, or selects the opposite member of an explicit branch pair. Prefix o+t+ch+l and t+o+ch+so are separately paid local realizations of the descending-event template. No unregistered rearrangement or general spelling law.
Within each listed exact group, parts fill its declared typed template. The 21 new parses are prospective local hypotheses, not outputs of a universal parser. All residual spellings remain literal.

Rows assigned to a clause form an ordered attribute bundle; bound x,H,r,I carry within the paragraph only. Complete formula is the conjunction of those bundles, not independent word-gloss substitution.

Text line order presents definitions, branch descriptions and a closing comparison; it is not claimed to be a literal temporal itinerary. C3 descent precedes C4 ascent in the narrated cycle, while C1 names both abstract branch types.
The reference-condition qo forms use the current base coordinate. This is not q morpheme export or an identification of qo with an independently known prefix.
ee is an extended baseline extent and eee the outermost grade. No letter-count-to-number law, numerical unit or source-hour equivalence is declared.

C5 introduces the common-midpoint equality constraint; b_lo and b_hi are the two already declared endpoints. The otherwise ambiguous okeey selects the upper member here by this paid complementary-boundary rule.
Completion dy supplies end time, d completion aspect, and am closure of whole interval. These are separate new units; their relation is explicit, not historical suffix knowledge.
The label .26 receives exactly the same generic index r as prose otor. Local label/prose reference identity is a C0 ownership commitment, with an unrelated/homonym rival retained.
Clauses and type arguments are exactly those itemized here; no unmentioned Sun, observer, calendar, named star, hour, period length, field-wide object identity or event frequency is supplied.

clauses.reading: The indexed height traversal is complete; the two reference boundaries are its paired endpoints.

whole_reading: Consider the marked object’s height relative to a reference boundary. Ascent and descent form opposed parts of one traversal. The index otor refers to that height trace: its opposed branch covers the extended range and returns to the lower limit. Descent begins, follows its branch and completes at the outermost lower point. Height then begins an extended ascent, reversing the completed fall and reaching the upper reference height. For the same index, the lower and upper limits stand at equal distances from a common middle point. The interval closes as one complete height traversal between the paired limits.

differential_consequence.versus_visibility: With fixed bindings, chteey predicts a positive height-change onset and choteey a negative height-change onset. A visibility reading instead predicts visibility onset/loss. Neither coordinate derivative implies visibility change without another occlusion/observer relation.
differential_consequence.concrete_countercase: A point ascending while remaining obscured satisfies the R ascent predicate while a visibility-onset predicate is false; a continuously visible descending point satisfies R descent while visibility-loss is false. These are hypothetical semantic countercases, not observed manuscript events or new control data.
differential_consequence.same_written_obligation: The same cheey must denote the H state and feed both onset templates; t/o retain one typed orientation rule. A later reading cannot replace H with visibility only in a favorable clause.
differential_consequence.RAW826: Pliny is source inspiration only. This positional candidate does not supply the source’s solar arrival/departure or first/last-visible-day interval statements and therefore is not an exact RAW826 rendering. No identity/copying proof follows.

To distinguish meaning on manuscript evidence, a separately admitted/owned positional-versus-visibility relation would be needed; this candidate itself introduces no reserve or engine action.
